Duration::where¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Duration Duration::where(const Series& mask, const Duration& other) const;

What It Does¶

Elementwise conditional selection: keeps self’s own value where mask is true, and replaces it with the corresponding position of other where mask is false. Read the call as “keep this value where the condition is true; otherwise use the replacement.” The receiver and replacement are not symmetric, so swapping them changes the result.

Important

Verify this direction before relying on it This convention is easy to get backwards when writing the mask. The example below is deliberately explicit about which positions end up as self and which end up as other, so you can check your own mask against it before trusting a where call that isn’t obviously symmetric.

Parameters¶

mask (const Series&)

A boolean mask, broadcast against self. Where true, self’s own value is kept; where false, the corresponding position of other is used.

other (const Duration&)

The replacement source for masked-false positions.

Returns¶

Duration A new duration: self where mask is true, other where mask is false.

Examples¶

Example 1. Replace every position past 4 days with a 99-day sentinel.

auto ranged = pluss::duration::range(
    pluss::duration::days(0), pluss::duration::days(10), pluss::duration::days(2));
auto mask = ranged.gt(pluss::duration::days(4));
std::cout << "mask=" << pluss::series::print(mask) << "\n";

auto replacement = pluss::duration::full({6}, pluss::duration::days(99));
auto picked = ranged.where(mask, replacement);
std::cout << "where=" << pluss::series::print(picked.total().days());

Output¶

mask=Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[false, false, false, true, true, true]
where=Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[99.0000, 99.0000, 99.0000, 6.0000, 8.0000, 10.0000]

ranged is [0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10] days; mask (ranged > 4 days) is [false, false, false, true, true, true]. At the three false positions (0, 2, 4), the result is other’s value (99). At the three true positions (6, 8, 10), the result is self’s own original value, unchanged.

Notes¶

  • mask is receiver-preserving: true keeps self, while false selects other. Remember it as receiver.where(mask, replacement) rather than as a symmetric selector.

  • fill_nat is the special case of where where mask is isnat() and other is the fill value.

See Also¶

  • fill_nat: the missing-value-specific special case of this operation.

  • isnat, isvalid: common sources for mask.
